newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-FRITZ STROBL FASTEST IN FINAL DOWNHILL TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FRITZ STROBL FASTEST IN FINAL DOWNHILL TRAINING.

text.p: Austria's Fritz Strobl confirmed his position as a gold medal contender for the men's downhill at the Alpine skiing world championships by posting the fastest training time on Friday.
Strobl, who also dominated Tuesday's first practice session on the Kandahar Banchetta slope, clocked one minute 52.59 seconds despite slowing before the final jump.
He was closely trailed by Luc Alphand in 1:52.84, while Italian favourite Kristian Ghedina was fifth with 1:53.47.
In Saturday's blue-riband race, Alphand will be bidding to become the first Frenchman to win a downhill gold medal since Jean-Claude Killy in Grenoble in 1968.
France's last world champion in the men's events was Michel Vion, now coach of the French ski team, who took combined gold in 1982.
Alphand, who has been on antibiotics since Monday to cure a bout of influenza, said he was feeling much better.
"The piste was quite uneven today but that's not surprising after four training runs and the combined downhill," said Alphand.

The 31-year-old Frenchman, who was an unlucky fourth in the 1993 world championship downhill and clinched bronze last year in Sierra Nevada, said: "If I come second tomorrow then that is no disaster."
Strobl, the only downhiller other than Alphand and Ghedina to have won World Cup races this season, was unaffected by his role as favourite.
"I have no problems being the favourite for tomorrow. I will not lose any sleep over it," said Strobl in his usual laid-back manner.
"I am pleased with my run today and will be pleased if I manage a good run tomorrow," he added. "Up in the starthouse, I told myself I would do a good training run and I did."
His compatriot and defending downhill champion Patrick Ortlieb said: "I don't mind if Fritz is considered the favourite. I didn't like being the favourite in Sierra Nevada."
Ortlieb clocked the 11th best training time with 1:54.04 but said he missed a gate to avoid piste workers.
The hefty Ortlieb did not have to fight for one of four Austrian starting bibs because the world champion qualifies automatically.
Strobl, his unrelated namesake Josef and Werner Franz had all qualified before coming to the north Italian resort.
Andreas Schifferer was third best on Friday in 1:53.16 to earn himself the fourth Austrian place over Hannes Trinkl, who was fourth fastest with 1:53.40.

A disappointed Trinkl said: "It will be awful for me to be sitting at home watching all the skiers from exotic nations. It is not fair that many of the world's best skiers cannot take part in the championships."
The fourth Swiss starting bib went to Markus Herrmann who completed the training two positions ahead of his team rival and 1993 downhill champion Urs Lehmann.
Herrmann will join compatriots William Besse, Franco Cavegn and the surprise silver medallist of Thursday's combined, Bruno Kernen, on Saturday.
